newsitem.title: USA: Fred Meyer to acquire Smith's Food for $2 billion.
newsitem.headline: Fred Meyer to acquire Smith's Food for $2 billion.

text.p: Fred Meyer Inc. said Monday it signed an agreement to acquire Smith's Food & Drug Centres Inc. for $2 billion, creating a supermarket and general merchandise retailing giant in the Western United States with annual sales of $7 billion.

Under the agreement, Smith's stockholders will receive 1.05 shares of Meyer common stock for each share of Smith's shares. Based on Friday's closing prices, the deal values Smith's stock at $43.97 each.
The $2 billion price tag includes $720 million in stock and the assumption of $1.3 billion of debt.
In late morning trading Monday, Smith's stock was up $2.50 at $42.50 on the New York Stock Exchange, while Fred Meyer was off 37.5 cents at $41.50, also on the NYSE.
"This merger of equals will create a merchandising powerhouse across the western United States," said Robert G. Miller, chairman and chief executive officer of Fred Meyer.

Under the terms of the merger agreement, which has been approved by the boards of both companies, Smith's Chief Executive Ronald Burkle is to become chairman of the combined companies, while Meyer Chairman and Chief Executive Robert Miller is to become president and chief executive.
Fred Meyer, based in Portland, Ore., is a regional retailer of general merchandise, food, apparel, jewelry, and home improvement products. It has 222 stores in 17 states.

Smith's Food is a regional supermarket and drugstore chain operating in the Intermountain and Southwestern regions of the United States. The company, which had 1996 revenues of $2.89 billion and employs more than 20,000 people, has 152 stores in Arizona, Idaho, New Mexico, Nevada, Texas, Utah and Wyoming.
The acquisition is expected to be completed by the end of the summer.
